top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a molecular design principle: a small molecule forms a ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase that nature does not make, so the protein is removed rather than inhibited. The chemistry is mature (two decades of independent reproduction, quantitative ternary-complex and cooperativity rules, wide use as a probe) and it opens targets no inhibitor can engage. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the heterobifunctional concept, and Handa's cereblon work explains thalidomide-type glues, so the citation covers the whole principle and not one molecular format. P003 (Ciulli in place of Handa) is a close second; P001 (Buchwald and Hartwig) is a clean, mature, well-credited prize I rank third.
